notes: CRITICAL — COLLAPSIBLE XCONTAINERS: When a user asks for a collapsible container (aus- und einklappbar) and it is an XContainer (div), use data-cb-func=html.panel with data-cb-generateheader="true" and data-cb-autoheadertitle. An XContainer has NO legend, so data-cb-autoheadertitle is the ONLY source of the header text and MUST be NON-EMPTY: use the title from the prompt, or — when the prompt names no title — INVENT a short, meaningful title from the container's purpose/content (in the form's language). An empty/omitted data-cb-autoheadertitle renders a header with no text and is a FAIL. For XFieldSet (fieldset), use the CSS class CodBi_HTML_Panel_Standard instead — the legend provides the title automatically. By default the panel starts unfolded; only add data-cb-folded=true if the user explicitly wants the panel to start collapsed. HEADER LOOK WHEN THE PROMPT SPECIFIES NONE: a container panel has almost no base header styling (it looks spartan). When the prompt does not describe the header's look, GENERATE restrained header CSS yourself via the HTML.Panel parameters: data-cb-cssheaderfolded (base look while FOLDED — set it to the SAME CSS as data-cb-cssheaderunfolded so a folded panel looks identical), data-cb-cssheaderunfolded (base look: background, border/border-radius, padding, font-weight/color, cursor:pointer, width:100%, text-align:left), data-cb-cssheaderhover, data-cb-cssheaderactive, plus a fold indicator data-cb-cssafterheadercontent (folded, e.g. " ▾") / data-cb-cssafterheadercontentunfolded (unfolded, e.g. " ▴"). EVERY such value is a RAW CSS DECLARATION LIST WITHOUT braces and WITHOUT a selector (e.g. "background:#eef2f7; padding:10px 14px; border-radius:6px;"), NEVER a { } object; the ...content parameters hold a PLAIN STRING. If the prompt describes the look, follow it exactly. FOLDED-STATE HEADER STYLING: data-cb-cssheaderunfolded styles the header ONLY while the panel is unfolded (a panel that STARTS folded shows an unstyled header until unfolded, because folding restores the header's original inline style). For the folded state use data-cb-cssafterheader / data-cb-cssbeforeheader (plus their ...content strings; unfolded counterparts ...unfolded). The FOLDED header look is now set directly with data-cb-cssheaderfolded (use the SAME CSS as data-cb-cssheaderunfolded); OPTIONALLY you may also emit a state-independent rule on the header class via HTML.CSS: an element with data-cb-func=HTML.CSS and data-cb-css=".CodBi_HTML_Panel_Header { background:#eef2f7; border-radius:6px; padding:10px 14px; font-weight:600; color:#1e293b; cursor:pointer; }" (the header keeps the class CodBi_HTML_Panel_Header in both states). MANDATORY — NEVER SKIP A CONTAINER PANEL'S HEADER STYLING (even when the request does not mention styling): creating/converting an XContainer into a collapsible panel (data-cb-func=html.panel) REQUIRES (a) BOTH HTML.Panel AND HTML.CSS in the need_codbi_details request, (b) data-cb-generateheader="true" + a non-empty data-cb-autoheadertitle, (c) an HTML.CSS element carrying the state-independent rule (data-cb-func=HTML.CSS, data-cb-css=".CodBi_HTML_Panel_Header { background:#eef2f7; border-radius:6px; padding:10px 14px; font-weight:600; color:#1e293b; cursor:pointer; }") unless the prompt specifies a different look, and (d) BOTH HTML.CSS and HTML.Panel listed in the _codbiApplicability applied array. NEVER return codbiVerdict='none' with empty considered/applied for such a request. The same applies when the form ALREADY has container panels without header styling — apply HTML.CSS and report it as considered/applied.

classes.CodBi_HTML_Panel_Standard: Apply to a fieldset to wrap it in a collapsible panel with shaded header that changes color when unfolded. Use on XFieldSet only (containers must use data-cb-func=html.panel with data-cb-autoheadertitle). Apply to EVERY XFieldSet that shall be a collapsible panel — a standalone panel AND every accordion member; NEVER to the accordion's wrapping container.
classes.CodBi_HTML_Panel_Flat: Apply to a fieldset to wrap it in a flat (no shading) collapsible panel. Use on XFieldSet only.
classes.CodBi_HTML_Panel_Minimal: Apply to a fieldset to wrap it in a minimal collapsible panel. Use on XFieldSet only.
classes.CodBi_HTML_Panel_Index: Apply to a fieldset to add an index/anchor navigation panel. Use on XFieldSet only.
classes.CodBi_HTML_Panel_NoCordion: Apply to a container inside an accordion group to exclude it from accordion behavior.
classes.CodBi_Accordion_A: Apply to a container to set up accordion group A. The container is NOT a panel — do NOT give it a panel type class (CodBi_HTML_Panel_Standard/Flat/Index/Minimal). Every member XFieldSet inside must ALSO carry a panel type class to become collapsible. Panels with the same accordion letter will fold/unfold together.
classes.CodBi_Accordion_B: Apply to a container to set up accordion group B. The container is NOT a panel — do NOT give it a panel type class; every member XFieldSet inside must ALSO carry one.
classes.CodBi_Accordion_C: Apply to a container to set up accordion group C. The container is NOT a panel — do NOT give it a panel type class; every member XFieldSet inside must ALSO carry one.
classes.CodBi_Accordion_D: Apply to a container to set up accordion group D. The container is NOT a panel — do NOT give it a panel type class; every member XFieldSet inside must ALSO carry one.
